bounded_leaf: Inspect only the exact generic client Peer send_request path used by rmcp-v3.1.4 tasks/get, tasks/update and tasks/cancel.

evidence: The three task client wrappers call Peer::send_request directly.
Peer::send_request delegates to send_request_with_option with no options, then to send_request_with_option_and_subscription.

The generic path invokes ServiceRole::enforce_request_association; its default returns Ok and RoleClient has no override in client.rs. No task-specific capability branch is present in this generic send path.
If an originating request exists, the generic path inserts OriginatingRequestId into Extensions; exact source documents this marker as non-serialized and never on the wire.

The path allocates request id/progress token, injects negotiated client request metadata into RequestMetaObject, extends _meta with PeerRequestOptions.meta when supplied, then sets progress token. The task wrappers use no options, so they add no wrapper-specific meta or extension rewriting.
finding.scope_limit: Generic Peer send-path contract only; concrete task request serde fields and server-side capability rejection remain a separate leaf.
finding.phase1_effect: No Phase-1 pass. Application correctness cannot rely on these wrappers for Tasks preflight; persistent execution and effect-safety obligations remain unresolved.
